subject: food-technology
title: MAP, Irradiation and Fermentation
welcome_lead: Modified atmosphere, gamma rays, and beneficial microbes.
meta_desc: A-Level Food Tech: MAP, irradiation, and fermentation.
final_note: Modern shelf life is a chemistry problem.

concepts.def: Modified Atmosphere Packaging — gas mix tailored to product.
Ionising radiation (γ, e-beam, X-ray) killing microbes.
Microbial conversion of sugars (lactic, acetic, alcoholic).
Live microorganism conferring health benefit (e.g. yoghurt cultures).
Preservation by salt, nitrites and/or smoke.

walkthroughs.body_html: MAP tailors gas: red meat (high O2 to keep red colour); fish/poultry (high CO2 to inhibit bacteria); salads (low O2, high N2 to slow respiration). Doubles or triples shelf life of perishables.
Irradiation uses gamma rays (cobalt-60), e-beam or X-ray. Approved for spices, herbs, frozen seafood in the UK (Food Irradiation Regulations 2009). Mandatory labelling with the 'radura' symbol.

Lactic acid bacteria ferment yoghurt, sauerkraut, kimchi, sourdough; Saccharomyces makes wine, beer, bread; Acetobacter produces vinegar. Fermentation preserves while adding flavour, texture and probiotic value.
